note: Illustrative reference script that exercises vivid action words. It tells an invented story and no claim here is sourced. Never publish a render of this fixture.

input.title: How a boom turns into a bust
input.viewerQuestion: Why do markets keep rising right up until they collapse?
input.audience: People curious about how markets behave

sections.heading: Opening hook
sections.purpose: Show a specific audience problem, immediate visual promise and central question.
sections.text: Every boom starts the same way. Prices climb, and everyone feels clever. Then one morning the stock market crashes. So why does it keep happening?

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.purpose: Establish relatable stakes, baseline and scope without repeating the hook.
sections.text: First, the bank prints more money. Cheap loans pour in from every direction. Unpaid bills pile up on the desk, and nobody looks at them.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.purpose: Explain the causal mechanism with sourced examples, not a generic list.
sections.text: The housing bubble inflates until it finally pops. Confidence shakes. Savings melt away, and the profit vanishes overnight.

sections.heading: Answer and takeaway
sections.purpose: Resolve the opening question and make the caveats explicit.
sections.text: Slowly, the market recovers. The regulator stamps its approval on new rules, and the company splits into two smaller businesses. The next boom is already on its way.
